title: Sequencing modules and how they relate
description: Connect sequencing and optical barcode workflows to phenotype scores, regression, experiment planning, power estimates, dose-response analysis and run comparison.
introduction: Start on Home with the question and the type of barcode data. Map Barcodes reads sequencing files; optical pooled screening reads registered image cycles through OPS. Both need an explicit mapping from barcode identities to the experiment. Regression relates compatible perturbation counts and phenotype scores; it does not replace barcode decoding. Experiment Design and Power belong before acquisition when you are planning the screen, while Dose-Response and Run Compare inspect suitable results afterwards.
conclusion: Keep sequencing references and plate layouts with the counts, and check the join to image-derived scores before interpreting a regression. Optical assignments require their own object join and aggregation; they are not automatically a drop-in sequencing count file. Treat planning assumptions, fitted effects and comparisons between completed runs as distinct results. The linked lessons and Home walkthroughs show the route for each kind of experiment.

map_barcodes.name: Map Barcodes
map_barcodes.guidance: Supply the references that encode your experiment. Inspect mapped counts and barcode QC before pairing well-level guide counts with phenotype scores.

produces.description: one row per read, with its three barcodes

declared_ports.summary: FASTQ reads to row / column / gRNA barcode assignments

barcode_qc.name: Barcode QC
barcode_qc.guidance: Inspect mapping depth, coverage, collisions and positional effects before guide-count filtering.

ops.name: OPS
ops.guidance: Use sequencing-cycle images and phenotype alignment to decode barcodes per nucleus. Aggregate/join the decoded identities to compatible phenotype inputs before Regression; the OPS database is not a drop-in FASTQ count CSV.

regression.name: Regression
regression.guidance: Match plate and well identifiers across phenotype and guide-count inputs, select the response and controls, and inspect diagnostics before interpreting hits. Direct measured responses are also supported.

declared_ports.summary: measurements plus a barcode map to gene-level hits

power.name: Power / Design
power.guidance: Estimate sampling needs from chosen effect sizes and variability; pilot measurements are optional evidence for assumptions.

experiment_design.name: Experiment Design
experiment_design.guidance: Enter conditions, controls, replicates and plate constraints, then export the experimental layout before acquisition.

dose_response.name: Dose–Response
dose_response.guidance: Supply dose and response columns, controls and units before curve fitting; this route does not require sequencing.

run_compare.name: Run Compare
run_compare.guidance: Compare compatible saved settings, counts and hit lists without treating changed input data as a controlled model comparison.

steps.action: Start on Home and open Mask. Load the example data, check channels and segmentation, then run.
Open Measure with the Mask project and create measurements and object crops.
Open Annotate, inspect representative objects and save phenotype labels.
Open Classify, choose images or measured features, and inspect held-out predictions.
Return Home and open Map Barcodes for the matching sequencing reads and references.
Open Regression with compatible phenotype scores and per-well guide counts; inspect hits and diagnostics.

optical_screen.title: An optical pooled screen

steps.action: Start on Home: open Mask, then OPS; supply original cycle/site images and phenotype alignment.
Join and aggregate decoded object identities with compatible phenotype responses before opening Regression.

optical_screen.note: Align & Stitch is optional when your images need tile-geometry inspection or coordinate mapping; it is not a prerequisite for the OPS example. A stitched image alone cannot replace the sequencing cycles. OPS tables require an explicit identity join/aggregation before regression; the walkthrough does not perform that conversion automatically.

steps.action: Start on Home with Experiment Design; assign conditions, controls, replicates and wells.
Open Power / Design and estimate sampling needs from explicit effect-size and variability assumptions.

connections.handoff: Pair guide counts with phenotype scores using consistent plate/well keys.
Check mapping and coverage before guide filtering.
Join/aggregate decoded objects to phenotype and guide inputs explicitly before Regression; this is not a direct CSV handoff.
Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design.
Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities.
Compare compatible saved result sets and their settings.
